In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a porous tube system to control the matric potential of soil and the effect of this on plant water status.
the development and use of a porous tube-soil- plant system to investigate water transport through the soil-root-leaf continuum.
the development of a system for controlling water availability in a soil-plant environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plant water status is a function of the soil water status, which is in turn controlled by the water potential in the porous tube.
the water transport pathway from the porous ceramic'soils' to the plant was not limited at porous tube water pressures up to -2. kPa.

the water potential in the porous tube was a reliable indicator of soil water potential, and that the soil matric and plant water potentials were not significantly affected until the tube water pressure was reduced to -2.5 kPa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the soil water status is a function of both plant water status and the soil water content, and that the soil water potential is a function of the water content.
the hydraulic properties of the soil and the plant are the major factors in determining water movement in a porous tube-soil- plant system.
water transport through the soil-plant-atmosphere continuum is controlled by the water status of the plant and the soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydraulic conductance of a plant-soil system is a complex function of the hydraulic properties of the soil, plant and the interactions between them.

the soil matric potentials of a porous ceramic 'bulk soil' were controlled by the porous tube water pressure and that the hydraulic conductance of a plant-soil-water system is dependent on both the hydraulic conductance and water potential of the soil and the hydraulic conductance, water potential and water availability of the plant.
water transport through porous tubes is a viable method to investigate plant water relations and water transport through a plant-soil continuum.
